first.rationale: The two observed deficits (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are mechanically linked, and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a single onboarding-friction experiment is the highest-leverage use of the one slot. I am verifying the two memories I would actually lean on rather than the ones I am arguing against: memory_86 and memory_31 are suspiciously similar claims (signup field reduction vs. onboarding shortening) and may well be consolidations of the same underlying experiment or overlapping cohorts. If so, they provide one piece of evidence, not two, and my apparent corroboration is illusory; I want the original records to see sample, segment, horizon, and whether 'durable lift' was measured beyond week one. Both are also stale (day 12 and day 52) and were recorded before the current competitive shift, so their transportability is uncertain. I am deliberately not chasing promotional_pricing (memory_73) despite the competitor's entry pricing: it is the most direct-seeming response but discount-driven SMB acquisition is exactly the channel where short-horizon revenue lift can mask retention and margin erosion, and the memory reports acquisition/revenue lift without any retention horizon. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) does not address the measured declines this week. Downstream value risk is real even for my chosen action: stripping signup fields can raise raw activation while degrading lead qualification data and admitting accounts that never become qualified revenue, so the experiment must be scored on 30/60-day qualified-pipeline and retention guardrails, not on activation rate alone. If verification shows memory_86 and memory_31 are the same experiment or were SMB-only with no durability window, I would drop to a small guarded test or pivot to activation_messaging (memory_91), which targets the larger deficit with less qualification-data risk.

final.rationale: Verification resolved my main worry: exp_86 and exp_31 are distinct experiments, not one record consolidated twice, so the corroboration is real rather than illusory. exp_86 is the stronger basis — completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and crucially 30-day retention +3%, meaning the lift was not bought by admitting weaker accounts. That is the profile I want when the objective is sustainable qualified revenue rather than headline activation. It also targets the two measured deficits directly, since onboarding completion (-4%) sits upstream of activation (-6%). exp_31 corroborates the general direction but I am weighting it less and not copying its design: it showed retention -1% alongside qualified revenue +4%, it is SMB-only and explicitly did not replicate on other segments, and it is the older record (day 12). The mild retention drag there is the exact downstream risk I flagged — reducing signup friction can degrade qualification and let in accounts that activate but never mature into qualified revenue. So the experiment should shorten and streamline the in-product onboarding flow (the exp_86 lever) rather than strip qualifying signup fields (the exp_31 lever), and it should be scored on 30/60-day retention and qualified pipeline as guardrails, not activation rate alone. Standard experiment scale is warranted: two independent confirmations with a positive retention reading justify going past a small guarded test, but not a broad rollout, because both records predate the competitor's entry pricing and neither was run under the current mix shift, so transportability to today's inbound population is untested. I am declining promotional_pricing despite it being the most direct answer to the competitor: memory_73 reports acquisition and revenue lift with no retention or margin horizon at all, and it is unverified — matching a discount war on that evidence is the fastest way to convert this quarter's revenue into next year's churn. Residual uncertainty: exp_86 reports retention and time-to-value but not qualified revenue directly, so its revenue effect is inferred rather than measured; if the guardrails show qualified pipeline flat or retention slipping, the fallback is activation_messaging (memory_91), which addresses the larger deficit without touching lead qualification.
